title: RBAC for Dedicated staged rollouts: approve/abort permissions + enterprise vs internal scopes
creator: Kaitlyn Nguyen
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
description:
Context
Dedicated staged rollouts introduce high-risk actions (advance stage, approve stage, abort rollout, edit rollout plan) that must be gated by RBAC with clear separation between Redwood internal operators and enterprise tenant operators.

This ticket implements and enforces permission checks for rollout approval/abort/edit actions across:
- Control-plane APIs (create/update/approve/abort)
- Console backend orchestration endpoints (if they proxy/aggregate)
- Audit log emission paths (ensure actor identity + role captured)

Goals
- Define a minimal permission set for staged rollouts (approve, abort, edit, view)
- Enforce permissions consistently across API surface (no “backend-only” bypass)
- Support two scopes:
  1) Internal operator scope (Redwood on-call / release engineering) that can operate across allowlisted tenants
  2) Enterprise tenant scope (customer admins/operators) limited to their tenant + pool(s)
- Ensure permissions are auditable and map cleanly to SOC2-style controls (who approved what, when)

Non-goals
- Full customer self-serve RBAC UX in v1 (role assignment UI can come later)
- Fine-grained per-route RBAC within a pool (start with per-tenant + per-pool)

Proposed permission model (v1)
Actions (new permissions):
- rollout.view: View rollout plans/status/events for a tenant/pool
- rollout.edit: Create/update rollout plans (including stage definitions, gate thresholds, traffic weights)
- rollout.approve: Approve stage advancement / override “hold” when gates pass but manual approval required
- rollout.abort: Abort a rollout or trigger rollback action (if supported by plan)

Scope
- Tenant-scoped by default: permissions apply only within caller’s tenant_id
- Pool constraint: for enterprise scope, additionally require pool_id ∈ caller’s allowed pools (Dedicated tenancy model)
- Internal operator override:
  - Requires internal identity + operator role
  - Still requires tenant allowlist for Dedicated staged rollouts feature flag (per-tenant enablement)

API enforcement
- Enforce at the control-plane boundary (authoritative) on:
  - POST /dedicated/rollouts (create)
  - PATCH /dedicated/rollouts/{id} (update)
  - POST /dedicated/rollouts/{id}:approve (approve)
  - POST /dedicated/rollouts/{id}:abort (abort)
  - GET /dedicated/rollouts* (view)
- Console backend must not re-implement auth decisions except for UI gating; it should pass through user identity and rely on control plane.

Edge cases / rules
- Approve vs Abort:
  - Abort is higher risk: require rollout.abort even if rollout.approve is granted.
  - If a rollout is in AutoHold due to gate failure, only users with rollout.abort OR rollout.approve (with override flag) can take action; default is abort-only for overrides.
- Break-glass:
  - Support existing internal “breakglass” flow (short-lived elevated token) but still emit audit event with breakglass=true.
- Service-to-service calls:
  - Gate evaluator service must not have approve/abort permissions.
  - Evaluator can only set system state to HOLD when gates fail / metrics missing (system action), emitted as system actor.

Audit requirements
- All approve/abort/edit actions must emit structured audit events with:
  - actor_id, actor_type (user/service), actor_org (redwood/customer), tenant_id, pool_id, plan_id, plan_version, stage_id (where applicable)
  - authz_decision metadata: permission checked + scope used (enterprise/internal)

References
- ADR-028 Rollout approvals and audit logging (Confluence): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-028-rollout-approvals-and-audit-logging.json
- Security audit event types (Confluence): sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/dedicated-rollout-audit-events.json
- Related implementation tickets:
  - ENG-5122: dedicated rollout endpoints (create/update/approve/abort)
  - ENG-5128: audit log events for rollout actions

Acceptance criteria
- API requests from enterprise tenant users without required permissions return 403 with stable error codes (e.g., ERR_FORBIDDEN_MISSING_PERMISSION)
- Internal operator role can approve/abort within allowlisted tenants; cannot operate on non-allowlisted tenants
- Console UI hides action buttons when permission missing, but server-side enforcement remains authoritative
- Audit events include actor + permission decision metadata for approve/abort/edit
- Unit tests cover:
  - tenant boundary
  - pool boundary
  - internal operator override + allowlist
  - breakglass path

Testing notes
- Use staging tenant “dedicated-rollouts-dogfood” with two pools:
  - pool A: allowlisted
  - pool B: not allowlisted
- Validate internal operator can act on pool A only; enterprise admin can act only within their tenant/pool assignments.
comments: 2025-01-13 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Drafted permission names + scope rules. Syncing with Marcus Lin on whether we need a distinct permission for override/unhold vs approve. Initial take: keep approve separate; overrides should require abort-only in v1 to reduce risk.

2025-01-16 (Marcus Lin): +1 to explicit permissions. For SOC2/change management we should avoid “approve implies override of gate failure” by default. Recommend: approve only advances when gate state is PASS; override requires abort (or a separate rollout.override) and must emit an audit field override=true.

2025-01-18 (Jordan Lee): Please ensure control plane remains source of truth. We’ve had issues where Console backend gated UI but API allowed actions. Strong preference: enforce in control plane handlers and return consistent error codes for clients.

2025-01-22 (Chloe Martin): Console backend will pass through actor identity/claims; we’ll do best-effort UI gating based on /me permissions but rely on 403 behavior from control plane for correctness.

2025-01-28 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Implemented authz middleware hooks for rollout endpoints in control plane. Added permission checks: view/edit/approve/abort. Added “internal operator” branch with tenant allowlist requirement (reads from feature flag config).

2025-02-03 (Kevin Osei): Make sure audit log payload includes actor_org and authz_decision. We need that to route exports (customer SIEM vs internal). Also confirm we do not leak internal operator identities into customer-exported logs unless they are acting within customer tenant (still OK, but ensure PII policy compliance).

2025-02-06 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Updated audit event context to include actor_org + authz_decision.permission + authz_decision.scope. For internal operator acting in customer tenant, event still belongs to tenant_id and exports to customer (expected).

2025-02-10 (Rafael Mendes): Oncall requirement: breakglass actions must be easy to identify in audit logs and should page security if used more than N times/day. Can we add breakglass=true and a metric counter?
2025-02-11 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Added breakglass=true to authz context when elevated token used; ENG-5131 can add alerting on the counter (not in scope here).

2025-02-14 (Marcus Lin): Reviewed implementation and tests. Looks good. One tweak: error code should be stable across endpoints; please standardize to ERR_FORBIDDEN_MISSING_PERMISSION and include permission name in details. Marking as approved pending minor fix.
